cards.body: Seismic appears to set the tone for this week's events in the hardware industry, and we've covered the biggest beats, including deeper dives on hardware and AI topics over on Tom's Hardware Premium . Stories this week are colored by the fact that Nvidia founder Jensen Huang has stepped away from his post as CEO. The ramifications are wide and far-reaching, as the company transformed from a gaming GPU manufacturer to an AI business over the past five years. First up, it's not only hyperscalers and neoclouds that have their eyes on AI. An increasingly popular segment among enthusiasts is PCs dedicated to running local AI models. With so many choices on the market currently, from the recently released RTX Spark to AMD's Strix Halo platform, we take a look at two unlikely contenders that are now going head-to-head: Nvidia's DGX Spark and Apple's Mac Studio. We ran a suite of real-world and synthetic benchmarks across both devices and tested large models on both machines. With prices at eye-watering levels, it's more crucial than ever that you make the correct choice for your intended workloads. Going deep on local AI performance benchmarking with Apple’s Mac Studio with M5 Ultra taking on Nvidia DGX Spark — inference engine recipes mandatory for bigger models as MLX stack matures DRAM capacity constraints have been an industry-wide sticking point as the AI buildout accelerates demand for dies. With costs spiraling across both client and enterprise hardware, AMD has shared further detail about MEXT, a predictive memory engine which aims to offer 99% of a server's performance while running on half the DRAM. Powered by a transformer model and clever use of flash storage, AMD is already running 145 servers with the system in place, with a view to expand that figure to 2,000 next year. AMD shares how it can retain 95% of server performance with just half the DRAM, sidestepping memory shortages with MEXT — tech powers over 100 servers already running, with plans to expand to 2,000 servers in 2027 Next, we sat down with Cognichip's Chief Product Officer in an extensive interview to explore how the company is rolling out AI-powered chip design tools. Back in September, the company revealed a suite of proprietary AI models, named Artificial Chip Intelligence (ACI), which are specifically developed for semiconductor engineering. While the tools have yet to be used in a shipping product, it could substantially improve chip development productivity by automating labor-intensive tasks. summary_data.subject_angle: Blackwell이 공식 수출 통제 대상임에도 **중국 AI 모델 학습에 실질적으로 활용**되고 있다는 정황은 Nvidia의 대중국 매출 전략과 미국 정부와의 관계에 정치적 부담을 더할 수 있으며, AMD 등 경쟁 칩이 동일 역할을 하지 못했다는 점은 CUDA/PyTorch 생태계의 독점적 지위를 역설적으로 입증한다.

cards.body: The topic of U.S. trade controls precluding the export of Nvidia and AMD high-end AI accelerator chips to China has taken a few twists lately. Jensen Huang's affairs aside, it's an open secret in the industry that Nvidia's Blackwell silicon finds its way into China, whether physically or virtually. UnemploymentLabs, an independent research outfit, has come up with strong evidence that those chips were used for training open-weight Chinese AI models, including DeepSeek V4, Kimi K3.1, MiniMax-M3, and Ling-3.1-Flash. The scientists are careful to hedge their findings, noting that while their math checks out, it does not reveal where the chips were, how they were accessed, or prove that export controls were broken. As far as we can tell, it's currently not illegal for Chinese companies to rent Blackwell hardware abroad, and even though Nvidia's grip is tightening , U.S. companies aren't strictly prohibited from doing so, as evidenced by the recent Tencent-Oracle deal . This identification method is limited to models with open weights, and depends on both hardware and software stacks used for model training — and yet it's both clever and simple, like the Egg of Columbus . (Image credit: UnemploymentLabs) Let's establish some base facts. First, different AI accelerator families have unique counts of shader modules (SMs), marginally analogous to CPU cores — Nvidia's Hopper chips have 132, Blackwell B series have 148, and Blackwell GBs come with 152. Second, while there's more than one software stack for training AI models, PyTorch and its CUDA-aware friends are by far the most widely used on the green team's hardware. The first step for training a model is initializing its weights, or how strongly the model considers each individual input. In modern LLM architectures, their initialization goes through a randomization step in which their values are adjusted plus/minus pseudo-randomly, using cuRAND — as in, randomly, but a seed starting value results in the same adjustment figures every time. As you'd expect, doing this for an entire model is a lot of computational work, so this process is spread out across all the SMs, further subdivided into threads. For large weight sets, the thread count per SM is 2,048 for Blackwell and Hopper silicon, and it's surely carefully chosen and optimized for. The researchers repeated a facsimile of the initialization process using the same chips, software, and thread counts. Using relatively simple statistical analysis, they spotted that their final statistical distribution of weight values precisely matched that of DeepSeek, Kimi, et al. As a test, they changed the SM and thread counts, and predictably, the correlation completely broke down. This let them pick out each family of Blackwell/Hopper chip used for each model, and eventually they also figured out an approximate count of cards used. cards.body: Introducing GR00T 2 We introduce GR00T 2, a new generation of foundation world-action models (WAMs). GR00T 2 predicts future video and robot actions together, learning how physical interactions unfold along with the actions that produce them. The models run on parallel grippers, dexterous hands, and humanoids. Learning to predict the world, not just act in it, unlocks three new capabilities. 01Emergence of X-Adaptability Skills shown only by humans, or with handheld and wearable devices, carry over to robots that never practiced them. - Human → robot. Shown the task only by humans, never on the robot, a robot with two five-fingered hands lines a lab funnel with filter paper and wets it with a wash bottle in 65% of trials. - Handheld UMI gripper → YAM. Shown only with a handheld UMI gripper, a different gripper from the robot's own, the YAM arm assembles a toy dump truck end to end in 60% of trials, a long-horizon task that takes up to 4 minutes. - Wearable hand → robot hand. Shown only with DexUMI, a wearable hand that mirrors the robot's fingers, a two-handed robot handles long-horizon dexterous work, such as preparing banana yogurt and scooping granola for breakfast, and highly dynamic tasks like striking a match to light a lamp. 02Fast Adaptation and Agentic Control GR00T 2 performs many new tasks zero-shot and masters them from a handful of demonstrations. Because it predicts the outcome it is acting toward, a reasoning model can also direct it. - Zero-shot generalization and few-shot adaptation. On 50 tasks never seen on the target robot, only in human video or on other robots, GR00T 2 succeeds 40% of the time zero-shot. Five demonstrations per task, under 3 minutes of robot data, raise that to 95% after a 30-minute fine-tune on a single RTX 5090. - Dexterity. With minimal post-training, GR00T 2 performs long-horizon, highly dexterous tasks with two 22-DoF Sharpa hands, such as seating GB300 memory modules (85%) and assembling a toy truck (65%). Previous models could not do these tasks. - Self-improvement. Reinforcement learning on the real robot lifts three contact-rich insertion tasks to 88–96% success. - Agentic control. With a reasoning model calling GR00T 2 through the WAM API, YAM completes 97 or more of 100 back-to-back assemblies of each of three toys, recovering from stalls and errors along the way. - Visual steering. When a reasoning model gives step instructions and marks where to grasp and release on GR00T 2's camera view, YAM follows what-and-where instructions 92% of the time, up from 40% with the task instruction alone, and finishes 17 of 20 long-horizon trash-sorting runs. 03Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation with GR00T 2 Turbo GR00T 2 Turbo is GR00T 2 built for speed. Despite the turbulence, the S & P 500 secured a weekly gain of 2.5%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq added 2.3%. Both indexes were up so much on Monday and Wednesday that declines on Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday were no match. In fact, both the S & P 500 and Nasdaq have made sizeable dents in the losses they suffered in the postelection market rout on Nov. 5. While Nvidia shares fell another 2% on Friday, the market ended the week under pressure for a different reason. It was the potential for multiple Federal Reserve rate hikes over the next few meetings that led to the selling. Before Friday's open, the October producer price index turned in its highest yearly reading in nearly four years. Headline PPI, a measure of wholesale inflation, was cooler than expected month over month. However, its year-over-year increase to 6.5% was all anyone cared about, especially after Tuesday's hot consumer inflation report . The Nvidia sell-off began Monday after reports that the chip giant's board was investigating CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China. The scandal escalated with reports that Huang had affairs with two Nvidia employees, culminating in his resignation Thursday. Longtime CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO, a move that Jim Cramer was pleased with. cards.body: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations. On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play important roles in the global AI industry. China China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday, a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang. Huang’s exit has also raised uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on Nvidia’s restricted processors, according to Reuters. Many of these chips are subject to U.S. export controls, making them difficult for Chinese companies to obtain. Singapore In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Singapore ministry said police took her passport to ensure she remained available for questioning, as she was not based in Singapore. The investigation examined whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration. In February 2026, police found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed offenses related to the suspected false declarations, according to the ministry. However, authorities said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. She was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore. Her passport was returned that month. Singapore also said it received limited assistance from U.S. authorities despite repeated requests for information about U.S. server maker Supermicro. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said its investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals remains ongoing. The ministry did not identify the six individuals or specify their alleged roles in the case. cards.body: Malaysia plans to introduce a new law requiring data center operators to disclose their AI accelerator imports and power consumption to prevent diversion of restricted hardware to countries like China and optimize the use of the country’s power infrastructure, reports Malay Mail . The authorities also plan to charge data center operators for unused electricity capacity they reserve. While the idea to use power consumption to detect potential GPU smuggling has merit, it also has flaws. Malaysia's Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani acknowledged on Thursday that some companies had rented space in Malaysian data centers to import GPUs legally, which they then shipped abroad in smuggling operations. To prevent such practices, Malaysia's Digital Ministry is now reviewing existing legislation to determine whether local authorities can take action against entities that re-export processors subject to U.S. export bans. The minister stressed that Malaysia wants AI accelerators imported into the country to be used domestically. The proposed legislation will require data center operators to disclose the number of GPUs they import, their power consumption (presumably nameplate power consumption), the physical locations of their facilities, and the identities of operators and hyperscale customers. The government intends to track data center operations throughout their lifetime rather than limit oversight to the project approval stage. Meanwhile, data center operators will have to pay for all the electricity capacity they reserve, irrespective of their actual power consumption. For example, if a data center secures 100 MW of power capacity but only uses 50 MW, its operator will still have to pay for the remaining 50 MW. The measure is meant to discourage companies from reserving electricity capacity they may not need for another one to three years. As an added bonus, the measure will further discourage rerouting AI hardware to China while pretending it is used in Malaysia. While data on power consumption could help Malaysian authorities spot suspicious discrepancies between AI GPU imports and actual data center operations, it is virtually impossible to accurately determine the number of AI accelerators deployed at a facility based on power consumption alone. For example, Nvidia's H100 and H200 SXM GPUs are rated at 700W, whereas its B200 SXM accelerators are rated at 1,000W, yet neither necessarily consumes its rated power under actual workloads. Furthermore, without knowledge of server configurations, the power consumption of CPUs, memory, storage, and networking equipment, or the power usage effectiveness (PUE) of a particular facility, any estimates of the number of operational GPUs would be imprecise, to put it mildly. Also, there may be a considerable delay between GPU imports and their actual deployment. Nvidia board urged to consider 'return of Jensen Huang' by two major investors

cards.body: Two major Nvidia shareholders are calling on the board of directors to weigh all options for the company's future leadership, including "the potential return of Jensen Huang." Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner posted a letter on X on Friday that urges Nvidia's board to "pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia." The letter is also signed by Atreides Management's Gavin Baker. Nvidia was Altimeter Capital's largest disclosed equity holding in its most recent SEC filing, with a 9.4 million-share stake worth nearly $1.9 billion as of June 30. Atreides held 1.2 million shares worth nearly $250 million at the end of June. The letter said Nvidia will be "capably led" by interim CEO Colette Kress, who served as Nvidia's CFO for 13 years before the board announced Thursday that she'd lead the company in Huang's absence. "But the Founder and long time incredible leader of this extraordinary company has earned the right for a deliberate process that avoids any needless rush to replace him before all the facts are known," the letter concludes. The document did not call for Huang's immediate reinstatement. Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday amid multiple affair allegations, including one with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, who also worked with Nvidia customer Megaspeed. The Singapore-based company is being investigated by the Justice Department for possibly redirecting some of its supply of Nvidia's restricted artificial intelligence chips to China. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said on X Friday that he signed a petition asking to reinstate Huang. A petition circulating online called "Stand with Jensen" claims to have more than 100,000 signatures, including more than 5,000 current Nvidia employees. Musk said on X Saturday that without Huang, some "critical deals will be lost." Another letter sent Friday called on U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick to testify about Megaspeed before the House Intelligence Committee. Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 about whether the Commerce Department is "properly performing its broader role of preventing China from acquiring advanced AI chips," according to the letter. Huang has also been asked to testify. The Commerce Department originally launched an investigation into Megaspeed that was moved to the Justice Department in 2025 after Nvidia's lawyer contacted a senior Commerce official, according to The New York Times. President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit China on Thursday, but doesn't plan to raise Nvidia and the suspected spy affair during his meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping, according to U.S. officials. Musk is expected to join Trump on the trip to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit on Nov. 18 and 19.

headlines.body: A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company’s recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang appears to have attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon. The petition website said the signers include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders. Notable supporters include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan. The petition states that its signers are “concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process” and demands that the board “bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts.” It also calls on the board to ensure a fair investigation and provide more information to the public. “Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice,” the petition says. Huang resigned on Thursday, four days after confessing to having an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. The former CEO has agreed to testify before Congress, while news reports have also suggested that Huang engaged in multiple extramarital affairs. Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as the company’s interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement. Nvidia’s stock price fell sharply through the week, while Huang’s departure is also expected to leave a big gap in AI industry funding.

headlines.body: When Jensen Huang quit, it struck me how quickly the conversation shifted from his departure to whether Nvidia could manage without him. It wasn't about whether the company had the technology, customers or talent to keep growing, but whether anyone else could do what Huang had been doing for the business. That made me wonder: did investors believe in Nvidia, or just Huang? The company is hardly short of capable people. Interim CEO and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been with Nvidia since 2013. Nvidia has experienced engineers, established customer relationships and a leading position in the artificial intelligence chip market. But, listening to guests on CNBC this week, I noticed how much of their concern was about the influence Huang had built outside Nvidia. On Friday, just a day after Huang quit, Dylan Patel of SemiAnalysis told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" how Huang would persuade executives at smaller companies that make critical components to commit capacity to Nvidia. This helped it secure "the majority of supply chain capacity," he said. Without Huang, competitors could try to persuade those suppliers to allocate more capacity to them, Patel argued. And so the big question is, how much of Nvidia's advantage comes from its technology and how much comes from the relationships Huang built? A rockstar CEO There are obvious benefits to elevating CEOs to be rockstars. They can attract investors, open doors and give a company a new identity. A charismatic leader attracts attention, reassures investors and makes a company's strategy easier to sell. Huang was particularly good at this. He helped shape the conversation about where AI was heading and made Nvidia central to it. Donning his trademark leather jacket, Huang took to stages around the world, courting world leaders to lay out his vision and explain why Nvidia would be at its center. Before Huang resigned, Eric Ross told "Squawk Box Asia" that Huang "is the company." That may sound like an endorsement, but it also helps explain why his departure has raised so many questions. Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon made an interesting distinction on the same program, also before Huang's departure. Nvidia had capable executives who could keep the business running, he said. What was harder to replace was Huang's vision. "They need a visionary like that," he said. But for a company whose valuation reflects not just what it sells but expectations of what AI could become, replacing that vision may prove harder than replacing the CEO. Duncan Clark pointed to another part of Huang's job. He had become a bridge between Silicon Valley, Asia and Washington, and one of the most prominent voices for the wider AI industry. "I don't think you can replace him with one individual," Clark said on "Access Middle East" on Friday. Replacing him with multiple people is "going to take time, and it won't be the same," he added. stage1.korean_summary: 현직·전직 직원과 주주 11만명이 Jensen Huang의 복귀를 요구하는 청원에 서명했다.

headlines.body: 불륜 의혹과 국가안보 논란으로 물러난 젠슨 황 전 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)의 복귀를 요구하는 목소리가 확산하고 있다. 황 전 CEO가 사임한 지 2일 만인 14일(이하 현지시각) 주요 투자자들이 이사회에 공개서한을 보낸 데 이어 온라인 청원에는 11만명이 참여했다. 14일 블룸버그통신 등에 따르면 엔비디아 주요 주주인 얼티미터 캐피털의 브래드 가스트너 CEO와 아트레이디스 매니지먼트의 개빈 베이커 창업자는 이날 엑스(X)에 이사회 수신 공식 서한을 공개했다. 6월 말 기준 두 회사는 엔비디아 주식을 각각 941만주(약 2조원)와 125만주(약 2700억원) 보유하고 있다. 이들은 즉각적인 복직을 요구하지는 않았으나 모든 사실관계가 확인되기 전에 후임자를 서둘러 선임해서는 안 된다고 주장했다. 조사 결과를 확인한 뒤 복귀가 주주 이익에 부합하지 않는다고 판단하면 이사회의 결정을 존중하겠다는 입장이다. 온라인 청원 ‘스탠드 위드 젠슨(Stand with Jensen)’에는 주주 약 6만명과 현직 직원 5000여명을 포함해 약 11만명이 서명했다. 일론 머스크 테슬라·스페이스X CEO는 엑스에 “엔비디아의 많은 계약이 서면이 아닌 젠슨과의 악수로 이뤄졌다”며 “그가 없다면 중요한 계약들을 잃게 될 것”이라고 적었다. 청원에는 팀 스위니 에픽게임즈 CEO, 개리 탄 Y콤비네이터 CEO, 에이든 고메즈 코히어 공동창업자 등도 이름을 올렸다. 패트릭 리우 엔비디아 자율주행 수석이사는 “젠슨의 지원이 없다면 자율주행과 실물AI(피지컬AI) 산업은 수년간 후퇴할 것”이라고 밝혔고, 위 팡 연구원은 과거 오픈AI 직원들의 샘 올트먼 복귀 요구 사례를 거론했다. 복귀 여론이 과열되면서 임원진을 사칭한 가짜 서한이 유포되는 해프닝도 벌어졌다. 13일 엑스에는 이언 벅 부사장과 빌 댈리 수석과학자 등이 황 전 CEO를 복귀시키지 않으면 스페이스X로 이적하겠다는 문건이 퍼졌다. 하지만 2023년 오픈AI 항의 서한의 이름만 바꾼 가짜로 확인됐다. 일각에서는 실리콘밸리의 복귀 요구가 국가안보 리스크를 경시한다는 비판도 제기된다. IT 전문 기자 카라 스위셔는 “국가 안보보다 돈을 우선한 주장”이라고 비판했고, 저술가 데스몬드 슘은 “미국의 수출 통제 위반 조장 사실이 밝혀진다면 뛰어난 업적도 행위를 정당화할 수 없다”고 지적했다. 이광영 기자 gwang0e@chosunbiz.com
